You are reviewing the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim (branch llamacpp) for STRUCTURAL refactor candidates.
First read /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md to understand the architecture.

HARD RULES:
- READ-ONLY. Do not edit, build, or run anything (no make, no scripts, no ./andesim). Baseline test runs are using the build tree right now. Use Read/Grep/Glob and read-only git commands only.
- Structural = behavior-preserving: dead code, duplication, needless complexity, stale comments/docs that contradict the code, naming that hides intent, repo hygiene. NOT rewrites for taste. The repo just went through a history cleanup, so it is fairly clean; report only what you can defend with evidence. An empty findings list is a valid answer.
- If you find what looks like a real BUG (behavior wrong), report it with category "bug-report" - it will be handled separately, not as a refactor.
- For every finding give: file (repo-relative), line, category, title, one-paragraph detail with EVIDENCE (what you read/grepped), safety (why removing/changing it cannot change behavior), verify_with (which existing test or check proves it after the change).
- Cite real file paths and line numbers you actually read. No speculation.

Your assigned scope (do not wander into other subsystems except to grep for references):
driver/ run path: cmd_run.cpp, run_plan.cpp/.hpp, process.cpp/.hpp, shm.cpp/.hpp, memmap.cpp/.hpp and any headers they own. Look hard at cmd_run.cpp (839 lines - the biggest file): long functions, repeated argv-assembly patterns, dead branches.

Return your findings as the structured output.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	// The phase-plan executor (F6) -- there is no QEMU2 handback leg.
2	// run_plan spawns each leg of a Plan in order,
3	// threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward (leg N's --handoff-out is
4	// leg N+1's --resume-from-qemu), and reports each leg's mcycle/minstret.
5	//
6	// plan_argvs is the pure core (no spawn, no mmap): it resolves each Step's
7	// engine + role against the registry and fills the invoke template with the
8	// threaded state paths, so the argv construction is unit-testable in isolation.
9	#ifndef ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
10	#define ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
11	
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
16	#include "plan.hpp"
17	#include "process.hpp"
18	
19	namespace andes_sim {
20	
21	// The framework-owned values shared by every leg of a run: the resolved
22	// shared-mmap path/size/base and the QEMU plugin path. Per-leg values
23	// (bin/state_in/state_out) are derived by plan_argvs from this + the threading.
24	struct RuntimeCtx {
25	  std::string mmap_path;
26	  long long mem_size = 0;
27	  std::string mmap_base = "0x0";
28	  std::string plugin_path;
29	  // QEMU `-readconfig` file matching the accurate engine's ISA, distilled from
30	  // its config.inc (the engine's `--print-qemu-config`). Empty => the fast leg
31	  // keeps its descriptor's default `-cpu` (engines without the flag; FA2).
32	  std::string qemu_cfg;
33	  // The QEMU CPU model the fast leg must instantiate ({qemu_cpu} fill),
34	  // parsed from the same probe's `driver = "<cpu>-riscv-cpu"` globals: the
35	  // readconfig globals only apply to THAT driver, and a mismatched model
36	  // silently ignores them (found live: andes-ax45mpv kept vlen=512 when the
37	  // ax66 run asked for 128). Empty => the family default (andes-ax45mpv).
38	  std::string qemu_cpu;
39	};
40	
41	// The family-default QEMU CPU model: the -cpu fallback when an engine's
42	// --print-qemu-config names none. One definition, used by the plan executor's
43	// {qemu_cpu} fill and by cmd_profile's engine-synced launch.
44	inline constexpr const char* kDefaultQemuCpu = "andes-ax45mpv";
45	
46	// hw-config sync: the QEMU fast leg models the hardware the accurate-leg
47	// engine measures, so its -cpu vlen follows that engine's descriptor. 512 is
48	// the fallback for engines that report none. One definition, used by both the
49	// plan executor ({vlen} fill) and the hybrid banner.
50	inline long synced_vlen(long engine_vlen) {
51	  return engine_vlen > 0 ? engine_vlen : 512;
52	}
53	
54	// A trigger's per-leg argv contribution, dispatched by the leg's role. The
55	// QEMU plugin takes its trigger as a comma-suffix folded INTO the one `-plugin`
56	// token (so it rides the `{trigger}` placeholder); vsim takes separate tokens
57	// appended to its argv. marker contributes nothing (plugin/vsim detect the markers
58	// themselves).
59	struct LegTriggerArgs {
60	  std::string plugin_suffix;        // qemu fast-leg: appended to {trigger}
61	  std::vector<std::string> extra;   // vsim accurate-leg: appended tokens
62	};
63	
64	// Map `t` onto `role`'s argv contribution. marker -> empty. pc -> qemu
65	// `,enter_pc=<enter_pc>` / vsim `--hybrid-exit-pc <exit_pc>`. Roles other
66	// than fast-leg/accurate-leg get nothing. A missing required param or an
67	// unknown trigger kind sets `err` (and returns an empty contribution).
68	//
69	// NOTE (altitude debt): these flag spellings are framework-side per-engine
70	// knowledge -- the one place F9 hardcodes a fast/accurate engine's CLI, unlike
71	// the base argv which comes from each engine's `--describe` invoke template.
72	// This is a deliberate scope cut: the principled form (per-(trigger,role) argv
73	// templates carried in `--describe`, filled by build_argv like `invoke`) would
74	// extend the F2 engine contract and is left for a later feature.
75	LegTriggerArgs leg_trigger_args(const Trigger& t, const std::string& role,
76	                                std::string& err);
77	
78	// Turn an accurate engine's `<bin> --print-qemu-config` probe into a QEMU
79	// `-readconfig` file under `workdir`. On a clean probe (exit 0, non-empty
80	// stdout) writes `workdir/qemu.cfg` and returns its path; on any failure
81	// (engine without the flag -> the parser throws -> non-zero exit; timeout;
82	// spawn failure; empty output; unwritable dir) returns "" -- the tolerant
83	// fallback that leaves the fast leg on its descriptor's default -cpu.
84	std::string stage_qemu_cfg(const std::string& workdir, const RunResult& probe);
85	
86	// The QEMU CPU model named by a `--print-qemu-config` probe's text: the first
87	// `driver = "<cpu>-riscv-cpu"` global, stripped of the "-riscv-cpu" suffix.
88	// "" when the text names none (probe failed / engine without the hook) -- the
89	// caller falls back to the family-default -cpu.
90	std::string qemu_cpu_from_cfg(const std::string& cfg_text);
91	
92	// Build every step's concrete argv, threading state files under `workdir`:
93	//   state_in[0]  = ""                       (cold start; no resume)
94	//   state_in[i]  = state_out[i-1]           (prior leg's drain)
95	//   state_out[i] = workdir/"state-<i>.bin"  (this leg's drain)
96	// Each step's engine is looked up in `engines` by id and its `role` template is
97	// filled via build_argv. Pure (no spawn). Returns one argv per step; on any
98	// error (unknown engine/role, unresolved placeholder) returns {} and sets `err`.
99	std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> plan_argvs(
100	    const Plan& plan, const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
101	    const std::string& workdir, const RuntimeCtx& ctx, std::string& err);
102	
103	// The exit code a leg returns after draining its state and handing off (the
104	// driver-side mirror of vsim's kExitHandoffToQemu). Every plan step is a drain
105	// step, so this is the expected per-leg exit.
106	constexpr int kDrainRc = 200;
107	
108	struct PlanOptions {
109	  int timeout_ms = 90000;     // per-leg spawn timeout
110	  int expect_rc = kDrainRc;   // drain success code
111	  std::string plugin_path;    // "" => $VSIM_PLUGIN else repo default
112	  bool dry_run = false;       // build argvs (incl. qemu_cfg) but spawn nothing
113	};

115	// Compose the "plan step N exited wrong" diagnostic. A drain step (expect_rc is
116	// the handoff/drain code) that exits 0 ran the ELF to completion without ever
117	// reaching its ROI boundary -- the marker/pc trigger never fired; say so and
118	// name the trigger kind so the fix (right ELF / right --trigger) is obvious.
119	// Any other mismatch gets the plain "expected X, got Y" line.
120	std::string plan_step_rc_error(size_t step, const Step& s, int expect_rc,
121	                               int got_rc);

123	// Execute `plan`: resolve the plugin, acquire the shared mmap (allocate one
124	// under /dev/shm when plan.mmap_path is empty, and own it), spawn each leg with
125	// a timeout, require exit == expect_rc, and read back each leg's mcycle/minstret
126	// from its drained state file. Returns the per-leg results; on the first failure
127	// `error` describes it and `phases` holds whatever completed before it.
128	PlanResult run_plan(const Plan& plan,
129	                    const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
130	                    const PlanOptions& opts = {});

132	}  // namespace andes_sim

1	// Subprocess helpers for andesim.
2	//
3	// run_process spawns a child, captures its stdout, and kills it after a
4	// timeout -- the primitive the engine registry uses to ask `<bin> --describe`
5	// and the plan executor (F6) uses to run orchestrated legs. F5 extends this
6	// file with exec_passthrough (inherit stdio, no timeout) for fast/cycle.
7	#ifndef ANDESIM_PROCESS_HPP
8	#define ANDESIM_PROCESS_HPP
9	
10	#include <functional>
11	#include <string>
12	#include <string_view>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	namespace andes_sim {
16	
17	struct RunResult {
18	  int rc = -1;                // child exit status, or -1 if killed/abnormal
19	  std::string out;            // captured stdout
20	  bool timed_out = false;     // killed because it exceeded the timeout
21	  bool spawn_failed = false;  // pipe/fork failed before the child ran
22	};
23	
24	// Run argv (argv[0] resolved via PATH), capturing stdout. The child's stdin
25	// is redirected to /dev/null; stderr too, unless relay_stderr is set, in
26	// which case the child inherits OUR stderr and its diagnostics stream live
27	// (used to surface the legs' leveled logs at --log-level <= debug). If the
28	// child runs longer than timeout_ms it is SIGKILLed and timed_out is set.
29	RunResult run_process(const std::vector<std::string>& argv, int timeout_ms,
30	                      bool relay_stderr = false);
31	
32	// Run argv to completion with the child INHERITING all three std streams
33	// (stdin, stdout, stderr) -- the transparent-passthrough mechanism behind
34	// `run --mode fast|cycle`: the engine reads/writes the terminal directly,
35	// so an interactive gdbstub or semihosting console works unchanged. No chdir,
36	// no capture, no timeout. Returns the child's exit code, 128+signal if it was
37	// signalled, or -1 on spawn failure / empty argv.
38	int exec_passthrough(const std::vector<std::string>& argv);
39	
40	// Fork a child that execs argv with inherited stdio and return immediately
41	// without waiting. Used by `run --mode cycle --gdb` to launch vsim in the
42	// background before exec-ing ICEman in the foreground. Returns the child pid
43	// on success, -1 on empty argv or fork failure.
44	int fork_background(const std::vector<std::string>& argv);
45	
46	// Run argv with BOTH stdout and stderr captured (separate pipes) and stdin
47	// inherited, streaming each complete line to `on_line(stream, line)` as it
48	// arrives -- stream is 1 (stdout) or 2 (stderr), line excludes the trailing
49	// newline. The callback owns presentation (it decides what to write to the real
50	// streams), so this is the filtered counterpart to exec_passthrough: same "run
51	// to completion, no timeout, propagate exit code" contract, but the parent sees
52	// every line. A final unterminated line is delivered too. Returns the child's
53	// exit code, 128+signal if signalled, or -1 on spawn failure / empty argv.
54	int run_line_filtered(
55	    const std::vector<std::string>& argv,
56	    const std::function<void(int stream, std::string_view line)>& on_line);
57	
58	}  // namespace andes_sim
59	
60	#endif  // ANDESIM_PROCESS_HPP

1	// Shared-mmap allocation for andesim.
2	//
3	// The caller asks for `size` bytes; we resolve a backing directory over a
4	// tier list (first fit wins, fit = size + 256 MiB free), allocate a sparse
5	// file with mkstemp+truncate, and print one status line that always names
6	// the chosen tier -- and, when we fell past /dev/shm, why. HSIM_MMAP_DIR
7	// pins a single tier (hard error if it does not fit; no fallback past it).
8	#ifndef ANDESIM_SHM_HPP
9	#define ANDESIM_SHM_HPP
10	
11	#include <functional>
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	namespace andes_sim {
16	
17	// Free-space headroom a tier must have beyond the requested size.
18	inline constexpr long long kMmapSafetyMargin = 256LL * 1024 * 1024;
19	
20	// One backing-store candidate: the directory plus the label used in
21	// status/error messages ("/dev/shm", "~/.cache/andesim", "HSIM_MMAP_DIR=..").
22	struct MmapTier {
23	  std::string dir;
24	  std::string label;
25	};
26	
27	// resolve_mmap_dir result: the chosen dir ("" on failure) and, when a tier
28	// was skipped, a human note saying which and why ("" when tiers[0] fit).
29	struct MmapDirChoice {
30	  std::string dir;
31	  std::string note;
32	};
33	
34	// Parse "8G" / "512M" / "1024" / "1.5G" into a positive byte count. On success
35	// returns the count and leaves `err` empty; on failure returns 0 and sets `err`
36	// to the argparse-style message. Fractional values truncate (1.5G -> whole
37	// bytes).
38	long long parse_size(const std::string& spec, std::string& err);
39	
40	// L26/F2: the physical shared mmap is one V-scratch page (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES)
41	// larger than the program's --mem-size, so the V-register transport page sits
42	// just ABOVE the program's declared RAM. No program layout -- low stack, top-of-
43	// RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling -- can reach a page past its own
44	// RAM, so the scratch can never be clobbered. The vsim side parks the scratch
45	// at the mmap's top page (v_scratch_gpa), which equals ram_base + program_bytes.
46	long long physical_mmap_bytes(long long program_bytes);
47	
48	// The largest --mem-size whose physical mmap still fits the 2 GiB AE350 DRAM
49	// window (program_bytes + scratch page <= 2 GiB). --mem-size is capped here.
50	long long max_program_mem_bytes();
51	
52	// First-fit resolver over `tiers`. `probe(dir)` returns the dir's free bytes,
53	// or -1 when it does not exist. A tier fits when probe >= size + margin.
54	// On success `err` is empty; when nothing fits, returns {"", ""} and `err`
55	// names every tier's reason plus the HSIM_MMAP_DIR hint. Pure: no env, no
56	// filesystem -- testable with a fake probe.
57	MmapDirChoice resolve_mmap_dir(
58	    const std::vector<MmapTier>& tiers, long long size,
59	    const std::function<long long(const std::string&)>& probe,
60	    std::string& err);
61	
62	// The andesim cache root: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim, else ~/.cache/andesim,
63	// else "" (no HOME). Shared by the mmap tier list and the repro bundles.
64	std::string andesim_cache_dir();
65	
66	// Build the real tier list from the environment:
67	//   HSIM_MMAP_DIR set -> that single pinned tier;
68	//   else            -> /dev/shm, then $XDG_CACHE_HOME|~/.cache + /andesim
69	//                      (created here so the free-space probe can see it).
70	std::vector<MmapTier> mmap_tiers();
71	
72	// WSL2 advice for `doctor`: given /proc/version contents, the repo dir, and
73	// the mmap tier list, return warning lines. Empty when not on WSL2. On WSL2:
74	// always the .wslconfig memory= hint (tmpfs is capped by the WSL VM), plus a
75	// drvfs warning for the repo or any tier dir under /mnt/ (slow, and
76	// MAP_SHARED is not coherent across the 9p boundary). Pure -- testable.
77	std::vector<std::string> wsl_warnings(const std::string& proc_version,
78	                                      const std::string& repo_dir,
79	                                      const std::vector<MmapTier>& tiers);
80	
81	// Convert a --mem-size spec into the fast leg's plain QEMU `-m` argv:
82	// {"-m", "<MiB>M"}. Empty spec -> {} with no error (QEMU as-is). Malformed
83	// specs and sizes that are not a whole MiB (QEMU's -m granularity) return {}
84	// and set `err`.
85	std::vector<std::string> qemu_m_args(const std::string& spec, std::string& err);
86	
87	// Allocate a sparse mmap file of `size` bytes in the resolved dir (mkstemp +
88	// truncate), print one "[hsim mmap] <size> at <dir> (free: <free>)" line
89	// (plus "; fallback: <why>" when /dev/shm was skipped), and return its path.
90	// On failure returns "" and sets `err`. Caller owns the file (unlink when
91	// done).
92	std::string allocate(long long size, std::string& err,
93	                     const std::string& prefix = "hsim-shm.");
94	
95	}  // namespace andes_sim
96	
97	#endif  // ANDESIM_SHM_HPP
98

1	// The hybrid guest memory map: which regions a workload may touch in
2	// `run --mode hybrid`, composed from the same sources the run itself trusts.
3	//
4	// Only hybrid-SUPPORTED regions appear (PM rule): regions modeled by BOTH
5	// engines whose content or device behavior the handoff actually provides.
6	// QEMU-only devices (MROM/PLIC/PLMT/virtio/...), vsim-reserved holes (PLDM),
7	// and unverified-parity devices (UART1/SMU) are deliberately absent.
8	//
9	// Sources, in provenance order:
10	//   - DRAM + V-scratch: the driver's own window math (--mem-size; the
11	//     reserved HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES page above program RAM, L26).
12	//   - ILM/DLM/HVM bases: the engine's `--print-qemu-config` text -- the same
13	//     staged qemu.cfg the QEMU fast leg boots with, so the printed bases are
14	//     exactly the run's effective geometry.
15	//   - ILM/DLM/HVM sizes + row presence: the engine descriptor's backdoor-gated
16	//     ilm/dlm/hvm_size (0 = content cannot cross the handoff -> row omitted).
17	//   - SimControl/HTIF + UART2: fixed AE350 platform constants, identical in
18	//     QEMU (hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c memmap table) and vsim (platform
19	//     memory_map.h); drift is guarded by tests/andes_sim/
20	//     test_andes_sim_print_memmap.sh, which cross-checks the engine's own
21	//     `--print-memmap` dump.
22	//   - L2C register window (0xe0500000): intentionally absent until an engine
23	//     ships with an L2C -- `--describe` carries no L2C capability today, and
24	//     every current engine is built _NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0.
25	#ifndef ANDESIM_MEMMAP_HPP
26	#define ANDESIM_MEMMAP_HPP
27	
28	#include <cstdint>
29	#include <map>
30	#include <string>
31	#include <vector>
32	
33	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
34	
35	namespace andes_sim {
36	
37	struct MemmapRow {
38	  std::string region;     // "DRAM", "V-scratch", "ILM", ...
39	  uint64_t base = 0;      // guest physical, first byte
40	  uint64_t end = 0;       // guest physical, LAST byte (inclusive)
41	  std::string transport;  // what the handoff does with the region's content
42	};
43	
44	struct MemmapResult {
45	  std::vector<MemmapRow> rows;
46	  std::vector<std::string> warnings;  // e.g. LM geometry unavailable
47	};
48	
49	// Extract the `riscv.andes.ae350.soc` [global] properties from an engine's
50	// --print-qemu-config text: property name -> value string, other drivers'
51	// globals (the CPU ISA block) excluded.
52	std::map<std::string, std::string> qemu_cfg_soc_props(
53	    const std::string& cfg_text);
54	
55	// Compose the hybrid map for `eng` with `mem_size` bytes of program RAM
56	// (--mem-size) and the engine's --print-qemu-config text (may be empty:
57	// LM/HVM rows are then dropped with a warning naming the missing probe).
58	MemmapResult hybrid_memmap(const EngineDescriptor& eng, long long mem_size,
59	                           const std::string& qemu_cfg_text);
60	
61	// "128M" / "4K" / "2G" for whole binary multiples, plain decimal bytes else.
62	std::string fmt_size(uint64_t bytes);
63	
64	// Render as an aligned text table (REGION/BASE/END/SIZE/TRANSPORT), warnings
65	// appended one per line.
66	std::string render_memmap(const MemmapResult& r);
67	
68	}  // namespace andes_sim
69	
70	#endif  // ANDESIM_MEMMAP_HPP
71

1	// The pure core of `run --mode hybrid`: turn the CLI selection into a Trigger.
2	//
3	// Split out from cmd_run.cpp so it is unit-testable without spawning qemu/vsim.
4	// pc-mode boundaries are resolved against the ELF .symtab here (via elf_syms),
5	// so the live path in cmd_run only has to build the 2-step plan and run it.
6	#ifndef ANDESIM_HYBRID_HPP
7	#define ANDESIM_HYBRID_HPP
8	
9	#include <string>
10	#include <vector>
11	
12	#include "cli.hpp"
13	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
14	#include "plan.hpp"
15	
16	namespace andes_sim {
17	
18	// Build the ROI Trigger for a hybrid run from `cli` + `elf` (the ELF is needed
19	// to resolve pc-mode symbol boundaries). The pc boundaries are stored as
20	// "0x"-prefixed hex in params (enter_pc/exit_pc). On a missing/unresolvable pc
21	// boundary or unknown trigger, returns a Trigger with empty kind and sets `err`.
22	Trigger hybrid_trigger(const Cli& cli, const std::string& elf, std::string& err);
23	
24	// Build the vsim accurate-leg's user-forwarded extra args (verbatim tokens
25	// appended after the trigger args): kanata ROI visualization
26	// (`--kanata <f> [--objdump <f>]`). vsim's own hybrid leg never executes
27	// anything outside the ROI (it resumes at the boundary and exits on the
28	// trigger), so plain `--kanata` already covers exactly the measured window --
29	// no separate "roi" flag exists on vsim's side. `kind` is the trigger kind,
30	// used to validate: --kanata is marker/pc only; --objdump requires --kanata.
31	// On a violation returns {} and sets `err`. Absent kanata yields an empty
32	// list (the common case). Post-`--` args are NOT forwarded here -- hybrid
33	// rejects them up front (cmd_run), as the handoff owns both legs' argv.
34	std::vector<std::string> vsim_extra_args(const Cli& cli, const std::string& kind,
35	                                         std::string& err);
36	
37	// ISA-sync guard for the accurate-leg engine: the hybrid fast leg is a 64-bit
38	// QEMU, so an engine reporting xlen != 64 cannot share architectural state
39	// with it. Returns "" when the pairing is valid, else the diagnostic. An
40	// engine that reports no xlen (0) is accepted as-is.
41	std::string hybrid_hw_check(const EngineDescriptor& acc);
42	
43	}  // namespace andes_sim
44	
45	#endif  // ANDESIM_HYBRID_HPP
46

1	// The phase-plan grammar driven by run_plan (F6), minus the dropped QEMU2
2	// step.
3	//
4	// A Plan is a list of Steps; each Step names an engine (by id, resolved against
5	// the F2 registry), the role to invoke it in (its `invoke` template key, e.g.
6	// "fast-leg" / "accurate-leg"), and a Trigger. run_plan spawns each leg in
7	// order, threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward, and returns each
8	// leg's mcycle/minstret. Under the no-QEMU2-handback design every F6 step
9	// drains, so the hybrid cycle figure is the vsim-leg mcycle minus the qemu-leg
10	// mcycle.
11	#ifndef ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
12	#define ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
13	
14	#include <map>
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
19	
20	namespace andes_sim {
21	
22	// The ROI delimiter for a step. `kind` is marker|pc; `params` carries
23	// kind-specific values (e.g. enter_pc, exit_pc) that F9 maps onto trigger
24	// args. F6 only exercises the default marker case (no params).
25	struct Trigger {
26	  std::string kind;
27	  std::map<std::string, std::string> params;
28	};
29	
30	// One leg of a plan: which engine, which invoke role, under which trigger.
31	// `extra_args` are verbatim tokens appended after the filled template and the
32	// trigger args -- the seam for user-forwarded per-leg flags (e.g. the vsim
33	// leg's --kanata), which are orthogonal to the trigger.
34	struct Step {
35	  std::string engine_id;  // "qemu" | "verilator:ax45mpv_premium"
36	  std::string role;       // invoke-template key: "fast-leg" | "accurate-leg"
37	  Trigger trigger;
38	  std::vector<std::string> extra_args{};  // default-init: keeps 3-field Step{} literals warning-free
39	};
40	
41	// A whole hybrid run. Every step loads `elf`; the shared mmap (`mem_size`
42	// bytes, at `mmap_path` or allocated by run_plan when empty) survives across
43	// every leg so memory threads through.
44	struct Plan {
45	  std::string elf;          // path to the ELF every leg launches
46	  long long mem_size = 0;   // shared-mmap size in bytes
47	  std::string mmap_path;    // "" => run_plan allocates one (F5) and owns it
48	  std::vector<Step> steps;
49	  // The engine whose hardware the fast leg(s) must model when the plan has
50	  // NO accurate-leg step of its own (the --verify oracle plan): the ISA sync
51	  // ({vlen}, {qemu_cpu}, -readconfig, LM sidecars) reads this engine instead.
52	  // Empty => derive from the plan's accurate-leg step (the normal case).
53	  std::string hw_engine_id;
54	};
55	
56	// What one drain step measured (read back from its state file), plus the
57	// leg's captured stdout -- the guest program's own output (UART/semihosting)
58	// rides the engine's stdout and must flow through to the user. `st` is the
59	// full drained record (verify_oracle F4: run --verify diffs the vsim drain
60	// against the oracle leg's in-process, after run_plan removed the files).
61	struct PhaseResult {
62	  unsigned long long mcycle = 0;
63	  unsigned long long minstret = 0;
64	  std::string out;
65	  hybrid_state_v1 st{};
66	};
67	
68	// Aggregate outcome. `error` empty => every step matched its expected exit and
69	// drained a valid state file; `phases` then holds one entry per step in order.
70	struct PlanResult {
71	  std::string error;
72	  std::vector<PhaseResult> phases;
73	  // The concrete per-step argv run_plan built (after placeholder fill, qemu_cfg
74	  // staging, and state threading). Populated whether or not the steps spawn, so
75	  // a --dry-run can print the exact commands without executing them.
76	  std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> argvs;
77	  // On a leg failure: where the kept evidence lives (the workdir's drain/
78	  // sidecar/cfg files, a copy of the ELF, manifest.txt). Empty on success or
79	  // when the bundle could not be written.
80	  std::string repro_dir;
81	  bool ok() const { return error.empty(); }
82	};
83	
84	}  // namespace andes_sim
85	
86	#endif  // ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
87

1	// andesim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andesim [<cmd>] [--mode M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// `run` is the default command: when the first token is not a known
9	// subcommand (and not a top-level help flag), the whole line parses as
10	// `run ...`, so `andesim --mode fast prog.elf` works without typing `run`.
11	//
12	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
13	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
14	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole
15	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
16	#ifndef ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
17	#define ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
18	
19	#include <string>
20	#include <string_view>
21	#include <vector>
22	
23	namespace andes_sim {
24	
25	// True for the known command names (run/list/doctor/profile). The single
26	// source of truth shared by the parser (default-command rule) and main's
27	// dispatch.
28	bool is_subcommand(std::string_view name);
29	
30	struct Cli {
31	  std::string subcommand;                 // e.g. "run", "list"; "" if none
32	  std::string model;                      // --mode fast|cycle|hybrid (field stays 'model': the concept, see list models)
33	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
34	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger marker|pc
35	  // Hybrid trigger args (empty => cmd_run applies the default). pc boundaries
36	  // are a symbol name or 0x address; the sizes stay strings here and are
37	  // parsed where they are used.
38	  std::string pc_start;                   // --pc-start (trigger pc)
39	  std::string pc_end;                     // --pc-end   (trigger pc)
40	  std::string mem_size;                   // --mem-size (guest memory; --mmap-size is a hidden alias)
41	  std::string runtime;                    // --runtime linux (proxy-kernel payload; "" => bare-metal ELF, the default)
42	  std::string kanata;                     // --kanata <file> (marker/pc ROI trace)
43	  std::string objdump;                    // --objdump <file> (kanata labels)
44	  std::string log_level;                  // --log-level 0..6 (vsim scale; "" => info)
45	  std::string log_file;                   // --log-file <path> (full trace capture)
46	  std::string step_timeout_ms;            // --step-timeout-ms (hybrid per-leg spawn timeout; "" => PlanOptions' 90000)
47	  std::vector<std::string> positional;    // non-flag framework args
48	  std::vector<std::string> passthrough;   // verbatim, everything after `--`
49	  bool help = false;                      // -h / --help (before `--`)
50	  bool dry_run = false;                   // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)
51	  bool print_memmap = false;              // --print-memmap (run --mode hybrid)
52	  bool verify = false;                    // --verify (run --mode hybrid)
53	  bool gdb = false;                       // --gdb (fast: QEMU gdbstub; cycle: vsim JTAG + ICEman)
54	  std::string gdb_port;                   // --gdb-port (fast: default 1234; cycle: default 9104)
55	  // profile's report knobs (values stay strings; cmd_profile applies the
56	  // defaults where they are used, like mem_size/gdb_port above).
57	  std::string limit;                      // --limit (profile; "" => 50)
58	  std::string min_iters;                  // --min-iters (profile; "" => 1)
59	  std::string addr2line;                  // --addr2line (profile; "" => auto)
60	  bool raw = false;                       // --raw (profile: dump the plugin log)
61	  bool llm = true;                        // --llm / --no-llm (profile report format)
62	  bool optimize_rvv = true;               // --optimize-rvv / --no-optimize-rvv (profile)
63	  bool no_source = false;                 // --no-source (profile: skip addr2line)
64	  bool has_passthrough = false;           // a `--` boundary was present
65	  std::string error;                      // non-empty => parse failed
66	};
67	
68	// Parse argv[1..] (program name skipped). The vector overload is the testable
69	// core; the argv overload adapts it for main().
70	Cli parse_cli(const std::vector<std::string>& args);
71	Cli parse_cli(int argc, char** argv);
72	
73	}  // namespace andes_sim
74	
75	#endif  // ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
